main_text.p: tradi solent, una à vera Dei Ecclesia, Altera à Platone, Tertia ab Aristotele.

p.i: Iustitia uniuersalis secundum Ecclesiæ doctrinam est integra conformitas motuum cordis, & omnium virium cum Deo seu cum lege Dei. Idem est enim dicere, congruere cum Deo, & congruere cum lege Dei, quia Deus talis est, sicut se in lege descripsit.

main_text.p: Plato iusticiam uniuersalem sic definit, ut sit obedientia omnium virium erga rectum iudicium rationis, id est, conseruatio ordinis diuinitus instituti.
Eandem definit Aristoteles esse obedientiam erga omnes leges honestas ad nos pertinentes, ut Aristides nominatur iustus, quia non violat ullam legem honestæ societatis, in qua versatur.

p.i: Descriptio iusticiæ à Clemente Alexandrino tradita, Δικαιοσύνη ἐστὶ κοινωνία [illegible, ~12 letters] μετὰ ἰσότητος, Iusticia est communicatio, qua Deus se nobis communicat, & est conseruatio ordinatæ æqualitatis, complectitur uniuersalem & particularem iusticiam. Ac prior quidem pars loquitur de prima tabula, & de actionibus diuinis in renatis. Altera vero de actionibus ordinatis erga proximum.

page.notes: The handwritten annotation "Axiomata theologica" in the left margin is manuscript, not printed, and is omitted. Ink strikethroughs cover "quia Deus talis est, sicut se" and "lege descripsit" in the first paragraph. The words are transcribed as printed. The strokes look like later manuscript cancellation. The Greek in the Clement quotation is only partly legible. The middle section is marked illegible and the opening and closing words are read from the scan with some doubt. The "K." and "K.I.", "K.II.", "K.III." markers and the "X." are printed section signs and are kept as paragraphs. No page number or running head is printed. "Etsi" at lower right is the catchword.
